newsitem.title: USA: Mexico sees further rises in PEMEX oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sees further rises in PEMEX oil exports.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Sunday he expected state-owned oil company Petroleos Mexicanos (PEMEX) to continue increasing its exports next year as it did during 1996.

"In 1996 the average oil exports rose by about 100,000 barrels per day over 1995 levels. For 1997, we expect PEMEX to increase its oil exports by another 100,000 to 150,000 barrels per day," Ortiz said at a conference on the fringes of the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

Ortiz told bankers attending a conference organized by the Institute of International Finance that Mexico had been underutilizing its oil resources and could improve efficiency through higher investment.
He added that other energy deals involving private sector investment in the petrochemical and natural gas sectors would move forward in 1997.
Ortiz attributed the delays in those projects to the legal and constitutional reforms which had to be carried out in order to open sectors previously reserved to the state to private investors.
On the other hand, he said Mexico was making great strides in attracting private capital to its telecommunications and public transport sectors.

Ortiz said that the Mexican government's focus shifted from privatization to improving the quality of Mexican infrastructure in order to offer the private sector a more efficient platform to compete in the global economy.
